letter.definition: A written message addressed to a person or organization.

envelope.definition: A flat (usually rectangular) container for a letter, thin package, etc.

postcard.definition: A card for sending messages by post without an envelope.

package.definition: An object wrapped or packed for delivery.

parcel.definition: A wrapped item sent through the mail or a delivery service.

stamp.definition: A carved or raised object used to print the same design repeatedly.

sticker.definition: A small piece of paper or plastic with an adhesive back.

label.definition: A brief description given for purposes of identification.

address.definition: (computer science) the code that identifies where a piece of information is stored.

return-address.definition: An address on a letter or package identifies the sender and shows where to send it if delivery is unsuccessful.

zip-code.definition: A ZIP code is a set of letters and numbers that helps postal workers sort mail.

tracking-number.definition: A unique code used to identify and follow the progress of a mailed parcel or letter.
tracking-number.exampleUsage: The receipt includes a tracking number for the parcel.

mailbox.definition: A private box for delivery of mail.

post-box.definition: A public box or container where outgoing letters can be deposited for postal collection.
post-box.exampleUsage: She placed the stamped letter in the post box.

slot.definition: A small slit (as for inserting a coin or depositing mail).

counter.definition: A calculator that keeps a record of the number of times something happens.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

receipt.definition: A written or digital record showing that a payment was made.

delivery.definition: The act of delivering or distributing something (as goods or mail).

pickup.definition: The attribute of being capable of rapid acceleration.

signature.definition: A person's name written in their own hand to show agreement or identity.

registered-mail.definition: Mail that the post office records and monitors to help ensure its safe delivery.

express-mail.definition: A faster postal service that gives priority to delivery compared with standard mail.
express-mail.exampleUsage: The clerk explained the expected delivery time for express mail.

certified-mail.definition: A postal service that provides proof that an item was mailed and usually records delivery or attempted delivery.
certified-mail.exampleUsage: The sender kept the certified-mail receipt.

postal-worker.definition: A person employed by a postal service to sort, handle, deliver, or assist with mail.
postal-worker.exampleUsage: The postal worker sorted parcels behind the counter.

mail-carrier.definition: A postal worker who delivers letters and parcels to homes and businesses.
mail-carrier.exampleUsage: The mail carrier delivered the parcel in the afternoon.

clerk.definition: To work as a clerk, as in the legal business.

postmaster.definition: The person in charge of a post office.

delivery-driver.definition: A worker who transports parcels or other items to their destinations.
delivery-driver.exampleUsage: The delivery driver loaded parcels into the van.

sorter.definition: A clerk who sorts things (as letters at the post office).

courier.definition: A person who carries a message.

customer.definition: A person who pays for goods or services.

mail-bag.definition: A strong bag used by postal services to carry or sort mail.
mail-bag.exampleUsage: The letters were placed in a labeled mail bag.

cart.definition: To transport something in a cart.

sorting-machine.definition: A machine that automatically separates and routes items according to information such as addresses or codes.
sorting-machine.exampleUsage: The sorting machine reads codes on envelopes.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.
scanner.exampleUsage: The scanner was used during the activity.

tape.definition: A strip of sticky material used to attach things.

bubble-wrap.definition: To surround an object with bubble wrap, protecting it from damage while it is stored or shipped.

packing-peanuts.definition: Small lightweight pieces of packaging material used to fill empty space and cushion items in a box.
packing-peanuts.exampleUsage: Packing peanuts protected the object inside the box.

box.definition: Private area in a theater or grandstand where a small group can watch the performance.

padded-envelope.definition: An envelope lined with cushioning material to protect the contents during shipping.
padded-envelope.exampleUsage: The small electronic part was sent in a padded envelope.

rubber-band.definition: A flexible loop used to hold things together.

ink-pad.definition: A small pad containing ink used with rubber stamps.
ink-pad.exampleUsage: The clerk pressed the stamp onto the ink pad.

date-stamp.definition: Applying a date stamp to a document or object records when it was created, received, or processed.

lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.

service-window.definition: A counter opening where customers speak to staff and receive a service.
service-window.exampleUsage: The customer brought the parcel to the service window.

po-box.definition: A numbered compartment at a post office stores mail for collection by its recipient.

loading-dock.definition: A raised platform beside a road or railway where cargo is transferred to or from trucks and trains.

sorting-room.definition: A room where letters and parcels are organized for dispatch or delivery.
sorting-room.exampleUsage: Mail is grouped by destination in the sorting room.

parking-lot.definition: An area with marked spaces where vehicles can be parked.
parking-lot.exampleUsage: The post-office parking lot is beside the entrance.

drop-off-area.definition: A designated place where items, passengers, or deliveries can be left.
drop-off-area.exampleUsage: The parcel drop-off area is near the main counter.

vending-machine.definition: A machine that dispenses products after a customer inserts payment.
vending-machine.exampleUsage: The vending machine was used during the activity.

form.definition: A category of things distinguished by some common characteristic or quality.

pen.definition: A writing implement with a point from which ink flows.

waiting-area.definition: A room in a place such as an airport or hotel where people sit until they are ready to leave or be served.

queue.definition: To form a queue, form a line, stand in line.
